<reason>B wins by distinguishing a durable, revisable commitment from aid that repeatedly expires. Multiyear funding and procurement provide meaningful predictability without freezing particular weapons allocations. A raises legitimate scarcity concerns but repeatedly assumes the motion requires irrevocability or prioritizing Ukraine in every emergency, rather than defeating B’s actual model. B also better explains the costs of uncertainty for planning, production, and Russian incentives. A’s claim that the absence of a decisive Russian breakthrough falsifies that mechanism attacks a prediction B never made.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s pressure-round answers dismantle A’s central dilemma: legislative amendment differs from routine expiration, and reallocating particular interceptors need not cancel broader assistance. A repeats the locked-resources-or-empty-promise binary without answering those distinctions.</best_rebuttal>
